Read all four proof steps, all thirteen dependency interfaces and the previously independently reviewed minimum-loop/Bowditch chain. The reduction used is existential for a shortest circle maximizing visits, not universal for every shortest circle. Empty spaces and CAT(1) components are handled before the non-CAT(1) supposition. A simplicial closed edge walk cannot have one edge, a two-edge walk is a backtrack with length-controlled contraction, and four edges cost >=2pi; hence exactly three distinct vertices remain. With a,b,c in [pi/2,pi), b+c>=pi>a gives strict triangle inequalities; s and s-a,s-b,s-c are in (0,pi), including the all-right endpoints. The determinant product is positive and Sylvester applies. Metric flagness fills this exact triple; positive Gram definiteness makes corner angles strictly between 0 and pi. For sufficiently small t with 2t<pi, cos(distance)-cos(2t)=sin^2(t)(1+cos(alpha))>0, so the available spherical shortcut contradicts local geodesicity. No global edge-cell distance equality is assumed except when justified by the chosen isometric circle. AC is inherited through attained short circles; all finite counting and determinant steps are choice-free. Davis I.7.4's final three-circuit argument agrees with this local proof.
